metaDescription: Seven freestanding propane patio heaters compared by BTU, burner build, base weighting, tank access and safety shutoffs, with fuel-use math for evening use.
expertTake: The Hykolity 50,000 BTU table-base heater is the best overall pick because the weighted table base steadies a tall tower and it carries a triple protection system. The Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU is the value pick with a known name and a 9 foot radius. Anyone with a covered porch, a low roof or a tight balcony should skip propane and buy an electric infrared heater.
introParagraphs: A freestanding propane patio heater is a tall burner with a reflector, a tank in the base and a lot of leverage on the person who tips it. It delivers more raw heat than any plug-in electric unit, which is why bars and decks still use them.

The real differences live in the burner, the base and the shutoffs. Cheaper units tend to save on base weight and shutoffs first. This guide looks at how each model is built, what the fuel math looks like for an evening, and which ones suit open space instead of a cramped corner.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU propane patio heater with sand box table base
products.description:
The Hykolity uses a double-layer 304 stainless steel burner grid and a conical barrel in place of the older round design. The listing highlights a table design base with a sand box, which means you can add weight to the foundation for stability. A tall heater is only as steady as its base, so a weighted base is a real engineering advantage.

It has a 50,000 BTU rating, wheels and tip-over protection. At that output a 20 lb tank runs roughly eight to ten hours on high, since propane holds about 21,000 BTU per pound and usable fuel is somewhat under the full 20 lb. The conical barrel is meant to improve stability and wind resistance.

The table surface adds practical use but takes floor area. Compared with the Amazon Basics heater it offers a higher BTU number and a weighted base, though it is a heavier assembly. Add sand only to the amount the manual specifies and keep the sand dry. Owners should leak-test the regulator connection with soapy water after every tank swap. Store the unit with the tank disconnected and the burner covered, and keep spare sand in a sealed bag so it never carries moisture into the base.
products.bestFor: Open patios where stability matters most.
pros: Sand box base adds weight for stability
Conical barrel resists wind better than a round one
cons: Heavy to assemble and move once filled

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU propane patio heater with triple protection
products.description:
This Hykolity variant stresses a triple protection system and a stainless steel burner in a table design. Press-button ignition lights it without a lighter, and the wheels make it easy to move from the garage to the patio. The listing also suggests uses beyond patios, such as balconies, camping and tailgating, though a propane tower is best kept on open ground.

Triple protection typically bundles a tilt shutoff, a flame-out device and an automatic gas cut, so a gust or a bump closes the valve. That package matters more than a few thousand BTU. It works the same way a pilot safety valve works on a water heater.

Compared with the sand box model it gives up the weighted base in exchange for a simpler build. It is easier to wheel around and quicker to set up. Treat the 50,000 BTU number as a ceiling and keep the control knob where you can reach it. The ignition button and the regulator are the two parts guests touch most, so check them before a party. Wipe the stainless with a mild soap, since cleaners with chlorine pit the finish over time.
products.bestFor: Buyers who value a documented safety package.
pros: Triple protection system named in the listing
Wheels for moving between storage and patio
cons: No sand box to weight the base
Tall tower still needs a perfectly level surface

products.name: Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU portable propane patio heater with wheels
products.description:
The Amazon Basics heater lists 46,000 BTU and heating up to a 9 foot radius, which is a realistic way to describe coverage: it warms a circle of seating, not a yard. It has one-touch ignition, an adjustable temperature knob and wheels, and it fits cafes and restaurants as well as homes.

Its base uses a water tank in the listing, a straightforward way to add ballast. Water is cheaper than sand and easy to drain for storage. Because water freezes, drain it before winter in cold climates.

Compared with the Hykolity it has lower output and a simpler interface. That makes it a straightforward pick for someone who wants a known retailer and a clear coverage figure. Check the burner for debris at the start of each season and tighten wheel bolts. If you store it outdoors, a cover is worth the small cost, since the paint is the first thing to chip in rain.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers who want a clear radius and simple controls.
pros: Coverage described as up to a 9 foot radius
Water ballast is easy to fill and drain
cons: Lower output than the 50,000 BTU models
Water ballast can freeze if left in winter

products.name: Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU propane patio heater with double-layer burner
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy uses a double-layer 304 stainless steel burner with a dual mesh structure. The mesh spreads the flame so the burner glows evenly instead of burning in tight blue cones. It lists 48,000 BTU, wheels and dual protection that cuts gas automatically.

The listing calls it a high-end auto shutoff design, which suggests flame-out and tilt protection, though the specifics are less detailed than on some rivals. Verify what is printed on the unit and in the manual.

Against the Hykolity it matches the burner material but lacks a table base. It is simpler and lighter on the floor. Keep the mesh free of ash and webs, and cover the unit through the off season. Because the mesh is what you see glowing, a patchy glow is the first sign of clogged ports. Burn it for a few minutes at the start of each season to clear the dust before guests arrive.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stainless burner without a table base.
cons: Safety specifics are less detailed in the listing

products.name: 50,000 BTU propane patio heater with adjustable heat focusing top
products.description:
This heater has an umbrella-style adjustable reflector that focuses warmth where you point it. Adjustable reflectors let you aim heat down toward seated guests, which can be more efficient than a flat top that radiates up and out. It also has a stable conical barrel that adds wind resistance.

At 50,000 BTU it shares output with the Hykolity models. The adjustable top is the difference: you tilt the reflector to cover a table instead of a whole deck.

It makes sense for a dining area. The listing is less detailed on certifications, so check the markings on arrival. Wipe the reflector with a damp cloth when cool, and keep the adjustment hardware free of rust. Set the angle before lighting, since reaching up to a hot reflector is a good way to burn a hand. Mark your preferred angle with a bit of tape so you can reset it quickly.
products.bestFor: Dining patios that want directed heat.
pros: Adjustable reflector aims heat at seated guests
cons: Less detailed safety documentation in the listing

products.name: GasOne 50,000 BTU stainless propane patio heater
products.description:
The GasOne pairs 50,000 BTU of radiant output with a stainless steel body and an adjustable heat control. The stainless construction is built for the weather and tends to hold its finish longer than painted steel. Wheels make moving it practical.

A heat dial lets you back off the output once the patio has warmed, which saves fuel. A 50,000 BTU burner at full output uses more than two pounds of propane an hour, so the dial pays for itself.

Compared with the Sweetcrispy it uses a similar stainless approach with a clearer dial. Check regulator fittings each season. Stainless still stains near a pool or the coast, so rinse it with fresh water and dry it. Heavy-duty usually also means heavy, so plan on two people for assembly and for lifting the barrel.
products.bestFor: Weather-exposed patios where finish durability matters.
pros: Adjustable heat dial controls fuel use
cons: Safety features are less detailed in the listing
Heavier to assemble than lighter models

products.name: CIAYS 50,000 BTU patio heater with sliding tank door
products.description:
The CIAYS is built around a side sliding tank door so you can swap the cylinder without wrestling with the base. It heats in 360 degrees at 50,000 BTU, and the listing claims about 30 minutes of assembly.

Tank swaps are the chore that owners dislike most, so a good door matters. A sliding door also keeps the tank out of view and out of the rain.

It competes with the Hykolity on output but lacks a table base. It is a practical choice for a deck where you swap tanks often. Keep the door track clean so it keeps sliding. A quick spray of dry lubricant in the track once a season helps. Also keep the tank upright and fully seated, since a tilted tank can starve the regulator.
pros: Side sliding tank door makes swaps easy
cons: Door track can jam with grit

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 90 inch tower with a 20 lb tank has a high center of gravity. The Hykolity sand box and the Amazon Basics water tank add weight where it counts. A wide, weighted base is worth more than a few extra BTU on a windy deck. Fill sand or water only to the amount the manual specifies, because overfilling strains the tank door and the wheel axles.

Look for a tilt shutoff and flame-out protection together. The Hykolity models list tip-over protection and a triple protection system, while the Sweetcrispy lists dual protection. A heater with a single shutoff is a poor buy for a deck. A tilt switch handles the bump, and flame-out protection handles the gust that blows the flame out while you are inside.

Propane holds about 21,000 BTU per pound, so a 50,000 BTU burner on high uses a little over two pounds an hour. A 20 lb tank therefore lasts roughly eight to ten hours. An adjustable dial, as on the GasOne and Amazon Basics, lowers the burn. Most owners find that medium output is enough once the seats have warmed, which can double the run time.

A double-layer 304 stainless grid, used by the Hykolity and Sweetcrispy, resists warping and holds an even glow. Cheap single-layer burners can sag over a few seasons. Check how the mesh is supported. A burner that rattles in shipping or on first light is a sign of loose support, which is worth returning for.

A propane patio heater is for ventilated outdoor spaces. Keep it well clear of awnings, umbrellas and branches, following the manual. Never use one on a covered porch or in a garage. Carbon monoxide has no smell, so the rule is about where the heater sits, not how it feels.

The CIAYS sliding door and the Hykolity table base show two approaches to reaching the tank. A tight base makes every swap harder. If you grill on the same deck and swap tanks often, easy access is a daily feature. Also check whether the tank can sit upright and whether the hose has slack, since a kinked hose is a common cause of weak flame.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared base designs, from sand boxes to water tanks to plain wheeled bases. Weighted bases ranked higher. A tower that looks stable in a photo can still wobble in a gust, so the ballast approach counted for more than appearance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety design
howWeEvaluated.description: We read for tilt shutoffs, flame-out protection and triple or dual protection systems. The Hykolity models were the clearest in their listings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fuel use
howWeEvaluated.description: We worked out burn rates from BTU, assuming roughly 21,000 BTU per pound of propane. Adjustable dials earned credit. A heater that can idle at low output is cheaper to run over a season than one that only has full blast.

howWeEvaluated.title: Burner build
howWeEvaluated.description: We examined stainless mesh and grid claims. Double-layer 304 stainless scored best.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered tank access, regulators and wheels, which wear first by year three.

cards.label: Sand
cards.text: The Hykolity sand box base holds sand, which does not freeze and stays put. It needs dry storage.

cards.label: Water
cards.text: The Amazon Basics water tank is easy to fill and drain but can freeze in winter.

howToChoose.note: Cold-climate decks pick sand; mild climates can use water.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A stable base, a table surface and a safety package that handles gusts.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Hykolity sand box and triple-protection heaters suit entertaining best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use the heater every weekend: the Hykolity sand box heater or the GasOne stainless build lasts.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use it a few nights each season: the Amazon Basics heater is enough.

maintenance.why: Gas leaks start at the threads. Brush soapy water and watch for bubbles.
Ash and webs block flame ports. Brush the mesh when cool.
Sand clumps when wet and water freezes. Drain or dry as needed.
Piezo igniters wear out. Replace a weak spark.
Rain rusts the base and burner. Cover once it has cooled.

faq.q: How long does a 20 lb tank last?
faq.a: At 50,000 BTU on high a tank lasts roughly eight to ten hours. Lower settings stretch that.

faq.q: Is a bigger BTU number better?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Wind and placement change the felt heat more than a few thousand BTU. A heater sheltered from the breeze and surrounded by close seating beats a stronger one in an open gap.

faq.q: Can I use it on a covered porch?
faq.a: No. Propane heaters need open, ventilated space and overhead clearance.

faq.q: Sand or water in the base?
faq.a: Sand does not freeze, while water is easier to drain. Either adds stability. Use the amount the manual states, and never leave water in a base through a hard freeze.

faq.q: How do I test for leaks?
faq.a: Brush soapy water on every connection after a tank swap and watch for bubbles. Replace any leaking part. If you smell gas, close the tank valve, move away and do not light anything until the leak is fixed.
A tilt shutoff combined with flame-out protection. Several models here list both. Neither replaces good placement, so keep the tower on level ground away from anything that can burn.
